raw_response.country: Multi-country (general discussion of developing-country cities with brief illustrative references to Argentina, La Paz, Manila, Jakarta, Casablanca, and South Africa/Durban)

criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and community drinking-water and sanitation service access in underprivileged urban districts (quartiers défavorisés) and informal settlements.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading topically: it explicitly discusses utility concession contract terms that fail to account for low-income ability to pay, municipal refusal to extend public services to informal settlements to avoid legalizing land occupation, prepayment meters, and cross-subsidy/social-tariff and social-connection rules directly governing service access. However, these mechanisms are only discussed conceptually in a corporate overview without empirical evidence, so both plain_criterion2_decision and the narrow decision are exclude (E05).
criterion_notes.c3: Fails Criterion 3: this 4-page article is a non-empirical corporate/practitioner policy overview summarizing reflections from an internal Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux working group report and book. It presents no research design, sample, primary data collection, empirical analysis, or systematic synthesis methodology.
criterion_notes.c4: No empirical access, connection, affordability, or continuity outcomes are measured or reported; the article only outlines general sector problems and lists commercial and technical options.
criterion_notes.c5: Does not report an empirical study population/sample, analysed exposure-outcome relationship, or empirical study design.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in French with an English summary; translation/comprehension directly from the provided French full text is straightforward and feasible per Criterion 10, though the record is excluded under E05 for lack of empirical evidence.

evidence_quotes.quote: Pour les populations n'ayant pas accès au réseau, les problèmes de disponibilité de l'eau et de coût du service se traduisent par une recherche constante d'une juste consommation:

Plusieurs mécanismes financiers sont présentés dans le rapport et visent à alléger les coûts supportés par les populations défavorisées : péréquation, tranche sociale, modalités de paiement, participation de la main-d'œuvre aux travaux, subventions, branchements sociaux, fonds de travaux, microprêts, prépaiement, tontines, etc.
Il visait essentiellement l'accompagnement des projets argentins, le recensement des expériences dans le groupe et hors groupe, ainsi que le recensement des solutions apportées.

Les discussions du groupe de travail ont fait ressortir un point capital : on ne peut pas aborder la question des quartiers défavorisés de la manière traditionnelle. On doit innover aussi bien dans l'approche du problème, que dans la mise en œuvre de solutions.

raw_response.exposure: Concession contract conditions, informal land tenure non-legalization policies, social tariffs/cross-subsidies, prepayment mechanisms, and differentiated technical service levels (discussed conceptually only)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). Although the article topically addresses water and sanitation access in low-income urban settlements (c1) and rule-type legal/institutional/contractual mechanisms such as concession contract rules, municipal refusal to recognize illegal land occupation via service provision, social tariffs, and prepayment (c2 under both plain and narrow readings), it is a brief practitioner/corporate overview summarizing an internal Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux working group reflection and book, with no empirical data, sample, research methods, or measured access outcomes.
